text:
Elaine: Noticed a spike of ephemeral CSR requests to signing-service in eu-west at ~03:12 UTC. Requestor shows 'proxy-provisioner' which is odd.
Kishore: Paste subject + thumbprint and which principal in audit?
Elaine: subject=CN=svc.proxy.edge.eu-west, O=redwood, SAN=proxy.internal; sha256=9a3f...
Elaine: audit snippet: ```2026-03-18T03:12:05Z INFO RequestReceived uid=6f2a authn=proxy-provisioner region=eu-west action=create_csr```
opsec-bot: alert: csr-anomaly(eu-west) — 6 events in 2m for subject pattern 'svc.proxy.edge.*' (rule: ephemeral-csr-spike). See /alerts/7423456789
Samir: We pushed a small RBAC tweak last night to give proxy-provisioner limited signing access for canary nodes at 02:45 — could be connected.
Kishore: I added that scoped allow. Intention was only CN matching 'canary-*' but I may have botched the glob.
Jason: Did the CA actually sign any of these, or were they queued?
Elaine: Two show signed==true with 1h TTL.
Kishore: Action plan: revoke issued certs, tighten RBAC, pull KMS decrypt logs for signing-key in that window.
Samir: Running revoke: ```./signingctl revoke --region eu-west --selector "subject:svc.proxy.edge*" --reason "ephemeral-csr-misissue"```
Elaine: Revoke finished — 2 certs revoked. Serials: 0x4a2f..., 0x4a30...
Jason: Forensics: get signing-service audit, KMS:Decrypt events (key_id=signing-key-eu-west), IAM:policy-change timeline, and edge-proxy request traces.
Kishore: GAIA audit query I'm running: ```SELECT * FROM audit_logs WHERE resource='signing-service' AND time >= '2026-03-18T02:40' AND time <= '2026-03-18T03:30' AND (action LIKE '%create_csr%' OR action LIKE '%kms:Decrypt%')```
opsec-bot: audit-query-result: 6 signing-service events, 3 kms:Decrypt by principal 'svc-kms-eu-mid'.
Samir: That kms principal is our regional signing agent — expected, but verify the principal maps to the intended service account.
Kishore: Short-term hardening: enforce server-side CN pattern checks in signing-service, require client cert binding for critical sign calls, and log caller token id + SNI + source IP.
Elaine: Proposed mitigations: rollback permissive RBAC, rotate signing intermediate or at least stop issuing from current intermediate, and add a live reject rule for CSR subjects not matching canary-*.
Jason: Prefer new intermediate signed by root KMS key to avoid full root rotation. Swap issuance to new intermediate.
Kishore: I'll open a rollback PR with a stricter IAM condition: ```Effect: Allow Action: signing:create_csr Resource: arn:.../signing-service/ca-1 Condition: StringLike subject: "canary-*"```
Samir: I'll collect the related logs and package evidence for incident. Elaine, can you pull edge-proxy traces (x-request-id) for those serials?
Elaine: On it. Will post to incident channel once ready.
Jason: Post-incident follow-ups: 1) add server-side CSR pattern checks 2) emit csr.requestor_identity & kms_key_id metrics to Prom 3) add auto-pause if >3 unexpected CSRs in 5m for a region.
Kishore: Add a CI policy test to validate IAM condition patterns pre-apply so globs don't slip.
opsec-bot: action_created: incident/7423456789 — Investigators assigned: @samir @kishore @elaine. Next update in 30m or on new findings. :lock:
